newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Busy first day for NZ's new electricity mkt - EMCO.
newsitem.headline: Busy first day for NZ's new electricity mkt - EMCO.

text.p: Trading was busy on the new wholesale electricity market when it opened on Monday, indicating widespread support from market participants, market operator EMCO (Electricity Market Company) said.
Buyers and sellers generated 51,300 orders and produced 22,700 different prices.
"The first day of business was in line with the trials we have been running in the lead up to the start of trading," EMCO chief executive Lincoln Gould said in a statement.
"Today was the culmination of considerable effort by the whole industry to establish this new market."
The market officially opens on Tuesday.
Day-ahead commitment prices for Tuesday, which indicate how spot prices will perform, ranged between NZ$36.80 per megawatt hour in the South Island and $42.00 and $44.90 in the North Island.

Previously quoted prices were in cents per kilowatt hour and did not include an Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) security charge, but EMCO said today's prices were in line with prices established under the old system.
The market trading and information system (COMIT) had performed up to expectations.
